m5: Liquidity. Volume measures the total value traded on a market since it opened; liquidity (Polymarket) or open interest (Kalshi) measures the amount available to buy or sell at a given moment. A deeper market aggregates the opinion of a larger number of participants, and its price is in principle less sensitive to a single order. A market whose cumulative volume stays below ${{thin}} is flagged as thin; this is the case for the runoff-qualification market, which trades thinly.

h1: Do markets see what the polls miss?
dek: L'Écart compares, on a daily basis, the implied probabilities of prediction markets with probabilities simulated from voting-intention polls. The divergence between the two measures is the object of this monitoring exercise.
stale: This data is more than two days old and may be out of date.
blackoutBody: French law (Act No. 77-808 of 19 July 1977) prohibits publishing election poll results the day before and the day of each round of the presidential election. Poll-simulated probabilities and market prices are therefore hidden until this period ends. See the legal notice.
blackoutMeta: Publication suspended during the election-silence period required by the Act of 19 July 1977. Data resumes once this period ends.

h2a: Two readings of the same race
subA: Each row compares, for one candidate, the market-implied probabilities against the probability simulated from polls: the mint marks give, column by column, Polymarket's own price then Kalshi's, never a mean; the black tick marks the polls. The gap is computed separately for each venue.

dvCap: Poll-simulated and market-implied probability of winning, by week.
dvSrc: Sources: polls from MieuxVoter/presidentielle2027; market prices from Polymarket and Kalshi, shown as data.
dvAria: Polls and market lines for {n}, with the gap between them
m1: Probability simulated from polls. Poll-derived probabilities are obtained by Monte Carlo simulation (20,000 draws); the sampling error applied grows with the candidate's score. Each draw selects one recent first-round poll at random, applies this error, and retains the two highest scores. The runoff outcome is drawn from the mean of the head-to-head polls available for that pairing, with an additional error term; pairings never polled are decided by relative first-round strength. Simulated probabilities assume each candidate's candidacy is confirmed.
m2: Uncertainty applied. Seven months before the vote, polls can diverge substantially from the result: five months before the first round of 2022, polls underestimated Jean-Luc Mélenchon by more than ten points. The "medium" level applies an error of approximately 1.5 points plus 20% of the first-round score, and of 6 points at the runoff. The uncertainty setting shows how sensitive the simulated probability is to this assumption.
m3: Market-implied probability. It combines prices from two prediction-market venues, shown separately and never blended into a mean. Kalshi is a regulated US exchange; it supplies only the winner contract's price. Polymarket is not authorised in France, where the Autorité nationale des jeux (ANJ) has blocked access since July 2026; it supplies both the winner contract's price and the runoff-qualification contract's price. When both venues price the same event, the page shows both prices (or the range they bound) rather than a mean. These prices, dated to the day of the last update, are shown as data, with no link to either platform, for academic research purposes only.
m4: Sources. Polls are drawn from the open MieuxVoter/presidentielle2027 repository (MIT licence), compiled from surveys published under the supervision of the Commission des sondages. Each poll remains the property of its institute and sponsor.
aboutP1: L'Écart is an academic research project, designed and built by Luke Segault. For the 2027 French presidential election, it compares the market-implied probability with the probability simulated from polls, to measure their divergence and examine its possible causes.
aboutOnly: For academic research only. This site does not constitute a forecast, advice, or an invitation to bet.
aboutContact: Contact: questions, corrections or data requests via GitHub.
